added_lemmas.statement: For every \(I\subseteq V\) and every pairwise disjoint \(A,B,C\subseteq V\), if \(\overline A\perp_{d,\mathcal G_{\mathrm m,I}}\overline B\mid\overline C\), then \(X_A\perp_{P_I}X_B\mid X_C\).

source.verbatim_statement: If \([A]\) and \([B]\) are d-separated given \([C]\) in the mixture DAG \(D_{\mu}\), then \(X_A\perp X_B\mid X_C\) in the mixture distribution \(p_{\mu}\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Saeed, Panigrahi, and Uhler (ICML 2020), Theorem 3.2; apply it to the post-intervention component DAGs, whose mixture DAG is \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm m,I}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The policy reads descendant membership from marginal oracle answers through the targeted-root descendant equivalence, which must be a declared direct proof dependency.

proposed.statement: For every \(\mathfrak m\in\mathfrak M_{n,K,d,0}\), there is a finite exact recovery policy using only targets of size at most \(d\). If \(d=0\), it outputs the empty oriented union without a paid query. If \(d\ge1\), the \(n\) singleton targets recover \(R_{\mathbf G}\) from \(t\in D_{\{a\}}(a)\). For each head \(t\), process its mixture ancestors with strict descendants before strict ancestors, maintain the already certified set \(P_t\subseteq\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(t)\), and query \(I=P_t\cup\{a\}\) for the next candidate \(a\); declare \(a\in\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(t)\) exactly when \(t\in D_I(a)\), and stop when \(|P_t|=d\). The policy outputs \(\mathsf T(\mathbf G)\) and uses at most \(n+n(n-1)\) paid queries.
proposed.justification: This verifies that the cycle-free endpoint uses the degree budget itself: certified parents block every indirect surviving path before the next source is tested.
proposed.gap: VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional gives the reverse-ancestor induction but does not formulate the resulting finite minimax recovery policy over the completed shared-kernel model class.
proposed.consumer: The feasibility theorem uses this policy to certify that panels of size \(d\), rather than \(d+1\), suffice whenever mixture ancestry is cycle free.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The decoder's observable descendant test is valid for arbitrary mechanism-variation sets by the targeted-root descendant equivalence, not by the full-oracle lemma restricted to \(\Delta=V\).

proposed.statement: Let \(r=\min\{d+1,n-1\}\). If \(s\ge r\), then \(N^{\star}(n,K,d,\tau,s)\le F(n,r,s)\le U_{\mathrm{PB}}(n,r,s)\). The decoder retains \(a\to t\) exactly when every cover row \(I\) with \(a\in I\) and \(t\notin I\) has \(t\in D_I(a)\); for every nonedge \(a\to t\), the cover contains such a row that also targets an \(r\)-set extending \(\{a\}\cup\operatorname{pa}_{\cup}(t)\).
proposed.justification: This is an explicit non-CADIM upper design that exploits last-parent blocking and works without knowing the union skeleton.
proposed.gap: CADIM scans ancestor layers with at most quadratic count, while single-DAG separating systems separate endpoints and do not enforce simultaneous parent blockers.
proposed.consumer: The bound supplies a concrete bounded-panel schedule whenever the exact adaptive frontier is computationally unavailable.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The generic binary realization proof uses the published I-mixture global Markov implication as its soundness half; because it proves existence of faithful positive parameters, the faithfulness and positive-weight assumptions are conclusions here and are removed as circular dependencies.

proposed.statement: Every finite graph family used for the feasibility, dense-endpoint, directed-tree, and cycle-free transcript lower bounds admits strictly positive binary component kernels \(\boldsymbol\kappa\), positive mixture weights \(\mathbf w\), and strictly positive shared target laws \(\mathbf q\) such that the induced laws \(P_\ell\), \(P_{\ell,I}\), and \(P_I\) satisfy \(\Delta(\mathbf G,\boldsymbol\kappa)=V\), every declared true edge is active in its child kernel, and simultaneous I-mixture faithfulness holds for every \(I\subseteq V\).
proposed.justification: A graphical lower pair is legally relevant to the population oracle only if compatible faithful mechanisms exist for all queried interventions.
proposed.gap: The anchor's local necessity examples and the presolve fixtures do not supply an all-parameter simultaneous-faithfulness theorem under padding and topology replication.
proposed.consumer: The theorem turns every graphical transcript adversary into a valid population-level impossibility result under the stated bridge.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The necessity witnesses require the declared simultaneous-faithfulness realization theorem to belong to the direct proof spine.

proposed.statement: For \(K\ge2\), \(n\ge2\), and \(1\le d\le n-1\), \(N^{\star}(n,K,d,0,s)<\infty\) iff \(s\ge d\); for \(1\le\tau\le n-2\), \(N^{\star}(n,K,d,\tau,s)<\infty\) iff \(s\ge\min\{d+1,n-1\}\). Also \(N^{\star}(n,K,0,\tau,s)=0\). Each necessity direction is witnessed by two legal models with \(\Delta=V\) whose complete oracles agree for every allowed target, and each sufficiency direction recovers \(\mathsf T(\mathbf G)\).
proposed.justification: The theorem identifies exactly when bounded interventions contain enough joint blocker capacity for union recovery.
proposed.gap: VariciKatzWeiSattigeriTajer2024Interventional proves a local size threshold but does not prove a full-oracle finite-versus-infinite minimax frontier or legal transcript indistinguishability.
proposed.consumer: A perturbation platform can rule out an intervention-size budget before collecting data and can identify the smallest multi-target panel size capable of exact latent-state union recovery.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The arbitrary-model upper bounds in the exact slices use the targeted-root descendant equivalence directly.

proposed.statement: The frontier satisfies the following exact reductions: \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,1,1)=n\); for two directed trees on three vertices, \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(3,2,1)=\infty\) and \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(3,2,2)=3\); and \(N^{\star}(n,K,n-1,n-2,n-1)=n\).
proposed.justification: These exact slices constrain any proposed general formula and expose both adaptive transcript packing and the dense complement-singleton endpoint.
proposed.gap: None of the cited mixture papers gives an exact total-intervention count even on these full-oracle subclasses.
proposed.consumer: The slices are regression tests for the general frontier and furnish small exact benchmarks for intervention-policy implementations.

open_obligations.what_is_open: An explicit evaluable all-parameter function \(Q(n,K,d,\tau,s)\) with matching universal-factor adaptive upper and legal full-oracle transcript lower bounds.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen primitives do not show that enough source-plus-last-parent blocker requirements coexist on one legal baseline transcript. Requirements obtained from different baselines cannot be combined in the transcript-packing lemma, while the cover upper bound need not be adaptively optimal.
open_obligations.attempted: The parent-blocking inclusion--exclusion cover gives a nonadaptive upper bound, and the transcript-packing lemma turns any one legal baseline family into a hitting-set lower bound. Dense chains and height-one unions make subsets of the requirements coexist, but neither construction realizes the general blocker cover under the simultaneous indegree and cyclic-complexity caps.
open_obligations.partial_result: The proved feasibility threshold is exact. Whenever \(s\ge r=\min\{d+1,n-1\}\), \(N^{\star}\le F(n,r,s)\le U_{\mathrm{PB}}(n,r,s)\); at the additional cycle-free feasible endpoint \(s=d\), a proved policy uses at most \(n+n(n-1)\) queries; and the dense endpoint has exact value \(n\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: The exact closed form of \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(n,K,s)\) for arbitrary \(n\), \(K\), and every feasible \(s\).
open_obligations.obstruction: Unique component paths bound each local blocker set but do not determine how blockers for different heads and components can be batched in one adaptive target. No frozen result supplies a single legal tree baseline whose changed-target families certify the required global lower count.
open_obligations.attempted: Centroid path splitting, complement-singleton panels, and source-swap transcript alternatives were checked. They close the three-vertex two-component instance but do not yield matching counts for arbitrary path overlap patterns.
open_obligations.partial_result: For two directed trees on three vertices, the proved values are \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(3,2,1)=\infty\) and \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{tree}}(3,2,2)=3\); complement-singleton panels also give an \(n\)-query upper bound when \(s=n-1\).

open_obligations.what_is_open: The exact closed form of \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,d,s)\) throughout \(s\ge d\).
open_obligations.obstruction: Reverse ancestral processing proves correctness at panel size \(d\), but its headwise candidate tests can overlap in transcript-dependent ways. The current legal lower alternatives do not certify that the resulting quadratic count, or any proposed batching improvement, is optimal.
open_obligations.attempted: Certified-parent blocking yields a policy with at most \(n+n(n-1)\) queries, and empty-baseline single-edge alternatives give an antichain-type lower constraint. For \(d>1\), these constraints do not force the simultaneous parent blockers used by the upper policy.
open_obligations.partial_result: Feasibility is exactly \(s\ge d\); a finite policy uses at most \(n+n(n-1)\) queries; and the indegree-one singleton slice is exactly \(N^{\star}_{\mathrm{cf}}(n,K,1,1)=n\).
